title: The promise never moves Part 2
author: Tshiamo Ramokgadi
body:
Holy Spirit, be with me as I minister these words to Your children.

As I put pen to paper today, I am sitting out on my porch, looking out into the stillness and reflecting on the last 24 hours. I’m back home right now, intentionally taking this time to slow down, catch my breath, and—as we famously say—bond with my family. It has truly been one of the greatest blessings. Indeed, no man is an island; we were never created to walk this life alone. We all need community in one shape or another.

Sitting here rewinding everything that has transpired over the last day, I find myself completely taken aback not just by the events themselves, but by the overwhelming, undeniable goodness of God.

To paint the picture: yesterday, we hosted our very first official group hike for the men of ididntknowiwasme right here in Johannesburg. Anyone who knows me closely understands why this hit my heart so deeply.

I remember coming to this exact same mountain three years ago. I was broken, battered, carrying a painful physical injury, and bound to so much internal weight. Yet even in that condition, sitting in my own mess, I felt His love and presence wrapping around me.

Fast forward to yesterday: I stepped foot on that very same mountain, but this time, I wasn't walking alone. I was standing alongside an entourage of mighty men of valor - six other guys who decided to step up and align with what God spoke to me on that lonely trail years ago.

I need us to just pause and let the gravity of that sink in.

Three years ago, God whispered a vision into my heart on a quiet slope. Years later, after carrying that mantle through seasons I couldn't even make sense of, I returned to the very place where it all started. Only this time, others were walking in the blessing of a vision I refused to give up on. The main message of my heart today is simple: I said yes. I took that first step in obedience when I was completely broken, and because of that single yes, today I get to carry other guys up the mountain with me.

Today, I want to come for someone.

I want to speak directly to the one who is terrified to pursue what God has called you to do. I want to speak to the one who doesn't believe they are worthy of being called. I want to speak to the one who feels far too messy or damaged to be used by God, to the one who has thrown in the towel because of the relentless opposition of life, and to the man or woman who has given up on that marriage, on those kids, or on that vision. This message is for you.

God is actively looking for people He can partner with to bring heaven down to earth. He is looking for those who will help manifest His will not just for our own comfort, but so that others can be set free. He is looking for ordinary young men and women, just like you and me, to be so completely sold out that we bring others along into what God has entrusted to us.

God wants to heal people through your story. God wants to release blessing and hope into communities through your simple obedience. In a society that is obsessed with self-exaltation, God is looking for men and women who will die to self, step up as fishers of men, and manifest what Christ wants to do on this earth. And the sobering reality is that He chooses to do it through ordinary people like you and me.

Even as we pushed through the strain to reach the top yesterday, I looked up and saw that the green chair was still there. The promise had not moved an inch. But this time, I wasn't sitting alone in the mist. I had a brotherhood standing beside me, guys looking out over the expanse of Roodepoort, realizing that reaching this summit was just the beginning of a whole new mountain range waiting to be conquered.

Your life was never meant to be lived just for you. It was meant to be offered as a living sacrifice so that Christ could shine through your story.

Before meeting Jesus, the disciples were just ordinary, flawed men going about their daily routines until they encountered an extraordinary God. If He could take a college dropout with a broken shoulder and use a single "yes" to build a brotherhood, imagine what He can do with your life if you just stop running.



The promise never moves. It’s time to say yes.

Love Mo!
